# 1 Enoch Chapter 91 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 91:3 — Register of the exhortation formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hearken aright to-the-voice of-my-mouth" | Archaic register preserves testamentary solemnity |
| LOGOS | "listen rightly to the voice of my mouth" | Modern equivalent; preserves dual command |
| PNEUMA | "hear every word your father speaks" | Compressed; loses the second imperative |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez has two distinct imperatives. EMET's 'hearken' is archaic without adding precision. PNEUMA's compression loses the command to attend correctly. Testamentary literature warrants formal language.

---

## 91:4 — 'double heart' vs. 'divided heart' vs. 'divided loyalties'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-double heart" | Literal: kilé lebb — 'two hearts' |
| LOGOS | "a divided heart" | Preserves body metaphor; natural English |
| PNEUMA | "divided loyalties" | Paraphrase; makes ethical import explicit |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Divided heart' preserves the Semitic body metaphor (cf. Psalm 12:2; James 1:8 dipsuchos) while being idiomatically natural. PNEUMA's 'loyalties' loses the heart imagery.

---

## 91:5 — 'chastisement' vs. 'punishment' vs. 'reckoning'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "chastisement" | Literal; carries corrective connotation |
| LOGOS | "punishment" | Standard English for penal judgment |
| PNEUMA | "reckoning" | Dramatic; implies accounting of wrongs |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'punishment' in most instances; retained EMET 'chastisement' in v. 7 where the corrective dimension is in view alongside wrath.

---

## 91:7 — Description of divine advent

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the holy Lord will-come-forth with-wrath and-chastisement to-execute judgment" | Compound hyphenated; preserves Ge'ez participial |
| LOGOS | "the holy Lord shall come forth in wrath and punishment to execute judgment" | Formal; clean English syntax |
| PNEUMA | "The holy Lord will march out in blazing wrath to judge the earth" | Dynamic; 'blazing wrath' adds vivid color |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS base with PNEUMA's 'blazing' rejected — adds color absent from the Ge'ez. 'Come forth' preferred over 'march out.'

---

## 91:9 — 'heathen' vs. 'nations' vs. 'nations'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "idols-of-the-heathen" | Older English term for goyim/ethne |
| LOGOS | "idols of the nations" | Neutral; standard modern rendering |
| PNEUMA | "Every idol the nations ever worshipped" | Paraphrase; 'ever worshipped' adds temporal sweep |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'nations.' 'Heathen' (EMET) carries pejorative overtones unnecessary in this context. PNEUMA's addition 'ever worshipped' is interpolated.

---

## 91:12–17 — Apocalypse of Weeks: formal vs. dynamic register

| Translator | Approach |
|---|---|
| EMET | Hyphenated constructs; solemn-archaic |
| LOGOS | Clean formal prose; week headings implied |
| PNEUMA | Narrative present; vivid ("sword is placed in its hands") |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS register for the prophetic schema. The Apocalypse of Weeks is a structured cosmic-historical account, not a dramatic narrative; formal prose is appropriate. PNEUMA's 'sword is placed in its hands' (v. 12) is vivid but acceptable as secondary variant.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
